topics: Atomic number, mass, shells and quantum numbers
Orbital filling and the periodic table
Space lattice, unit cell and crystal systems
BCC, FCC and HCP: numbers, APF and lattice-parameter relations
Surface defects, eutectic freezing and single crystals
Constitutional supercooling and special solidification processes
Strain energy, dissociation and stacking faults
Climb, cross-slip, interactions, Frank–Read sources and pile-ups
Grain refinement and the Hall–Petch relationship
Fick's second law and the error-function solution

learningObjectives.description: Explain the scope of physical metallurgy and the composition–processing–microstructure–properties relationship.
Distinguish atomic number, mass number, proton count and neutron count.
Determine maximum electron capacities of shells, subshells and orbitals.
Interpret principal, azimuthal, magnetic and spin quantum numbers.
Apply the Pauli exclusion principle to electron occupancy.
Classify elements as metals, metalloids and non-metals using periodic-table position and characteristics.
Apply orbital-filling order and electron-configuration rules.
Relate transition-metal electron configurations to variable valence and chemical behaviour.
Explain ionic, covalent, metallic and secondary bonding mechanisms.
Compare primary and secondary bonds by strength, directionality and physical origin.
Relate bond type and directionality to conductivity, ductility, brittleness and cohesion.
Identify bonding within and between the layers of graphite and in diamond's covalent network.
Explain dipole interactions and hydrogen bonding as secondary bonding.
Identify equilibrium interatomic spacing from the minimum of a potential-energy curve.
Relate potential-well depth and curvature to cohesive energy, melting temperature and elastic modulus.
Explain thermal expansion through anharmonicity and asymmetry of the interatomic potential.
Distinguish the individual attractive and repulsive forces from their zero resultant at equilibrium.
Interpret the attractive and repulsive terms in a mathematical interatomic potential and the condition for short-range repulsion.
Explain the space-lattice concept and identify the role of a unit cell in generating a crystal.
Interpret lattice parameters, crystal-system constraints and the three-dimensional Bravais-lattice classification.
Compare BCC, FCC and HCP by atoms per unit cell, coordination number and atomic packing factor.
Derive contact directions and lattice-parameter–atomic-radius relationships for BCC and FCC.
Identify BCC, FCC and HCP structures, their close-packed stacking sequences and their implications for packing.
Use the ideal HCP axial ratio and interpret deviations in real HCP metals.
Use standard crystallographic notation for directions, direction families, planes and plane families.
Determine Miller indices from plane intercepts, including parallel and negative intercepts.
Calculate interplanar spacing for cubic crystals and relate it to lattice parameter and atomic radius.
Relate close-packed planes and directions, equivalent plane families and available slip systems to deformation behaviour.
Define and calculate linear and planar atomic density.
Locate octahedral and tetrahedral interstitial sites and compare their number and relative size in common crystal structures.
Explain interstitial carbon accommodation, local lattice strain and carbon solubility in ferrite and austenite.
Relate supersaturated interstitial carbon to martensite tetragonality.
Describe the sequence and crystal structures of iron allotropes.
Explain the FCC-to-BCC transformation in iron, carbon-solubility changes and martensite formation by quenching.
Apply Bragg's law to calculate X-ray diffraction angles from wavelength and interplanar spacing.
Explain the geometric origin of the path difference in Bragg diffraction.
Compare established routes for producing consolidated metallic products, including solidification, electrodeposition and powder metallurgy.
Distinguish nucleation from growth and explain their sequential roles in solidification.
Explain homogeneous and heterogeneous nucleation and identify preferred nucleation sites.
Construct and interpret the free-energy change of a spherical solid embryo, including surface and volume terms.
Calculate critical nucleus radius and homogeneous nucleation barrier from interfacial energy and volumetric driving force.
Relate undercooling to the volumetric free-energy driving force, critical radius and nucleation barrier.
Apply contact-angle and shape-factor concepts to heterogeneous nucleation and grain-refiner selection.
Compare temperature dependence of nucleation and growth rates and identify grain-size control variables.
Distinguish stable, metastable and labile temperature zones relative to the melting point.
Interpret pure-metal cooling curves and explain thermal arrest through latent-heat release.
Explain recalescence and distinguish latent heat from sensible heat.
Explain planar-interface instability and dendrite initiation during solidification.
Identify dendrite arm geometry, orientation and primary/secondary/tertiary branching.
Explain constitutional supercooling as a solute-boundary-layer and liquidus-gradient effect.
Relate cooling rate and dendrite arm spacing to microstructural refinement and homogenisation distance.
Explain grain multiplication through detachment of dendrite arms.
Identify chill, columnar and equiaxed zones and explain their formation in ingots.
Relate pouring temperature, mould temperature and thermal gradient to ingot grain structure.
Explain mould-corner effects and the influence of geometry on solidification structure.
Distinguish liquid, solidification and solid-state contraction and relate them to feeding and pattern allowances.
Explain piping formation, hot-top feeding and the risks of secondary piping.
Distinguish interdendritic shrinkage porosity from gas porosity and blowholes.
Explain gas sources, degassing and pressure-tightness implications of pore morphology.
Compare killed and rimming steels by deoxidation, gas evolution, shrinkage compensation and internal defects.
Explain why rimming steel can provide a clean, ductile surface suitable for deep drawing and how blowholes behave during rolling.
Distinguish normal, inverse, gravity and microsegregation by mechanism and spatial distribution.
Identify macrosegregation examples and explain density-driven crystal segregation.
Explain homogenisation of microsegregation and assess limitations due to diffusivity, arm spacing and macrosegregation.
Identify common casting surface defects and relate them to their causes.
Calculate the critical distance or thermal-gradient condition for constitutional supercooling.
Explain metallic-glass formation as suppression of crystallisation by rapid cooling.
Describe special solidification and crystal-growth processes, including Czochralski growth and zone refining.
Explain investment casting and identify its applications and limitations.
Explain the role of mould and core permeability in removing gases during casting.
Distinguish alloys, solid solutions and multiphase metallic materials by phase count and crystal structure.
Differentiate substitutional and interstitial solid solutions and identify their atomic arrangements and strain effects.
State and apply the four Hume–Rothery factors governing substitutional solid solubility.
Use crystal-structure, atomic-size, chemical-affinity and relative-valence compatibility to assess complete solid solubility.
Classify intermediate phases as valency compounds, interstitial compounds and electron compounds.
Relate characteristic compositions or electron-to-atom ratios of electron compounds to their crystal structures.
Read binary phase diagrams using horizontal tie lines to determine the compositions of coexisting phases.
Apply the lever rule to calculate liquid and solid phase fractions in a two-phase region.
Interpret phase fractions geometrically and identify the majority phase from tie-line distances.
Explain the sequence of equilibrium solidification in an isomorphous alloy using liquidus and solidus compositions.
Explain why equilibrium solidification requires diffusion in the solid to maintain compositional uniformity.
Explain constitutional supercooling through solute partitioning, the liquid concentration boundary layer and the local liquidus temperature.
Relate constitutional supercooling to planar-interface instability, cellular/dendritic growth and columnar-to-equiaxed transition.
Define the equilibrium partition coefficient and interpret solute rejection or enrichment at the solid–liquid interface.
Predict how thermal gradient and interface growth rate affect planar-front stability.
Explain coring as intragranular composition variation caused by limited solid-state diffusion during non-equilibrium solidification.
Interpret solute redistribution during non-equilibrium solidification, including freezing-range changes and successive solid-layer compositions.
Explain peritectic surrounding/enveloping and the isolation of an untransformed core by a product-phase shell.
Explain homogenisation of cored alloys, its purpose and its practical limitations.
Distinguish overheating from burning by the effective local solidus, grain-boundary liquation, reversibility and material damage.
